published_statement: Abstract (p.1): 'We find in all cases studied that the energy density fluctuations are large whenever the local energy density is negative. This is taken to mean that the gravitational field of a system with negative energy density, such as the Casimir vacuum, is not described by a fixed classical metric but is undergoing large metric fluctuations.' Sec. III.B (p.9), squeezed states |alpha,zeta> = D(alpha)S(zeta)|0>: 'Our primary concern is whether or not Delta << 1, which is best determined by numerical evaluation of Delta using Eqs. (3.2), (3.18), and (3.19). The figures illustrate the results. For states which are sufficiently close to coherent states, i.e. r << |alpha|, we do indeed find that Delta << 1. However, as the magnitude of the squeeze parameter r increases relative to that of |alpha|, we find that Delta increases. By the point that the state is sufficiently squeezed to have rho = <:T00:> < 0, we always have that Delta is at least of order unity. Thus squeezed states for which the energy density is negative exhibit large energy density fluctuations.' Fig. 2 caption: '... gamma = delta = 0 and theta = pi/2 ... Note that Delta << 1 only when s >> r, the region of classical behavior. Otherwise, Delta ~ 1.' Sec. III.A (p.6): 'the condition for the expectation value of energy density to be negative is cos(2theta) > sqrt2 eps. In this case we have Delta(x) > 1.' Sec. III.C (p.12): 'Delta' >= 1/2, Delta >= 1/3 (3.45). This means that the dimensionless Casimir energy density fluctuations are always at least of order unity.' Sec. V (p.16): 'states of a quantized field in which the mean energy density is negative SEEM to exhibit large energy density fluctuations. This was illustrated in our model calculations for squeezed states and for the Casimir vacuum state.'
published_hypotheses: H1 massless minimally coupled scalar, FLAT spacetime, box of side L with periodic b.c. (2.1)-(2.6)

H2 the measure is KF (3.2): Delta(x) = |(<:T00^2(x):> - <:T00(x):>^2)/<:T00^2(x):>|, coincidence limit, 00 component, every operator (including the quartic :T00^2:) normal-ordered against the Minkowski vacuum -- a POINTWISE measure

H3 'cases studied' = four: (i) vacuum+2 single-mode superposition (2.15), (ii) the two-parameter squeezed COHERENT family D(alpha)S(zeta)|0>, alpha = s e^{i gamma}, zeta = r e^{i delta} (3.9)-(3.19), (iii) its alpha = 0 limit, the squeezed vacuum (3.22)-(3.23), (iv) the Casimir (periodic-z) vacuum (3.24)-(3.45)

H4 for (ii) the conclusion is drawn from NUMERICAL evaluation of (3.2) with KF's own (3.18) and (3.19), on plotted slices (Figs. 1-2: gamma = delta = 0, theta = pi/2, over (r, s); Figs. 3-4: delta = 0, s = 1/2, theta = pi/2, over (r, gamma)) -- not a proof over the family
H5 'large' / 'at least of order unity' is not quantified by a threshold; the abstract's 'in all cases studied ... whenever' is universal, Sec. V's 'seem to exhibit' is hedged
H6 for (i) the inequality is drawn from KF's (3.8); for (iv) from (3.43)-(3.45) under the Wick condition and a diagonal <:d_A phi d_B phi:>

rederivation.outcome: ALL CHECKS AS REPORTED: True (17 s; log rederive/gr-qc_9304008-qualitative-conclusion.out). Independent of fluctuation.py (nothing imported from the tree). C1: exact normal-ordered moments of D(alpha)S(zeta)|0> from the normal-ordered generating function in KF's conventions (3.12)-(3.17) reproduce KF (3.18) exactly (control). C2: exact <:T00^2:> differs from KF's printed (3.19) (agrees with the tree's KF_319_IS_EXACT = False). C3: on KF's own Fig. 1/2 slice (gamma = delta = 0, theta = pi/2) rho = 2K(2s^2 - (1-e^{-2r})/2) and <:T00^2:> = 4K^2(m^4 + 6 m^2 g + 3 g^2) with m^2 = 2s^2, g = -(1-e^{-2r})/2; on the curve s^2 = (1-e^{-2r})/8 (every r > 0): rho = -K(1-e^{-2r})/2 < 0 AND <:T00^2:> - rho^2 = 0 identically, <:T00^2:> = K^2(1-e^{-2r})^2/4 > 0, so KF's Delta = 0 EXACTLY at a negative-energy point. Witness r = 1, s = 0.32876: rho = -0.432332 K. C4: independent control by truncated Fock matrices (numpy/scipy expm, dim 220, tail weight 2e-25): rho = -0.4323323584 K, <:T00^2:> = 0.1869112681 K^2, Delta = 4.5e-16. C5: KF's printed (3.18)+(3.19) at the same point give Delta = 0.9976. C6 (z3, one-quadrature reduction T00 = u^2, the exact form for a single plane-wave mode since d_x phi = -d_t phi): rho<0 AND Delta=0 SAT (model m = 1, g = -2), rho<0 AND Delta<1/10 SAT; alpha = 0 gives Delta = 2/3 (negation UNSAT); in t = -g/m^2 (rho<0 <=> t>1) Delta<1/10 exactly for t in (1.97802, 2.02899), Delta<1/3 for t in (1.94281, 2.15470), <:T00^2:> < 0 for t in (1, 1.81650). C7: over the slice box r in (0,2], s in (0,1], of the rho<0 cells 0.90% have Delta<0.1, 3.6% Delta<1/3, 27.4% Delta>1. C8: the other three cases hold: vac+2 rho<0 => 1/3<Delta<1 (z3 negation UNSAT, vacuity guard SAT); squeezed vacuum 2/3; Casimir 6/7.

later_literature.ref: A. Perez & D. Sudarsky, 'Renormalization of the Quantum Stress Tensor Fluctuations and the Limits of Semiclassical Gravity', arXiv:2512.17789 v2 (2026)
later_literature.what: Confirms the zero-mean half: 'for any vacuum or squeezed vacuum state |0_x>, Delta T^2 = 2<T>^2' (their (20)), i.e. Delta = 2/3, and 'squeezed vacua ... fail to satisfy the natural semiclassicality criterion'; says its results 'agree in general lines' with Kuo & Ford. For coherent displacements on top of a vacuum of energy -hbar tau/(12 pi) (2D, locally freely-falling normal ordering) their (18) makes semiclassicality (Delta T^2 < <T>^2) require T_cl > hbar(5+sqrt26)tau/(12 pi), i.e. POSITIVE total energy -- in tension with the exact single-mode result here. As read from the text layer, the cross term of their (16), +(hbar/2pi)<:T:>tau, has the opposite sign to Wick's theorem for a displaced Gaussian state (which gives -(hbar/2pi)T_cl tau = +6 g T_cl, the form verified here by Fock matrices, C4); with the Wick sign the 2D criterion would read T_cl^2 - 2gT_cl - g^2 > 0, which admits negative total energy. Recorded as a DISCREPANCY, possibly a dropped minus in the text layer; their App. C (C29) not read; different model. Not quoted as an error.

lacked_data: KF lacked no physical datum: the conclusion rests on no measured constant (K_00 cancels in Delta; C1-C3). What they lacked, for case (ii), was the correct quartic moment: their numerical evaluation used their printed (3.19) (H4, p.9), which is not the exact <:T00^2:> (C2; tree KF_319_IS_EXACT = False). With the exact moment the conclusion MOVES for the squeezed coherent family: on the surface <:T00^2:>-connected = -2x(mean-field part) (t = 2; on KF's own Fig. 1/2 slice the curve s^2 = (1-e^{-2r})/8) Delta = 0 exactly at rho < 0 (C3-C4), and Delta < 1/10 on a thin band around it (t in (1.978, 2.029); 0.9% of the rho<0 cells of the slice box). Evidence the other way, equally computed: the conclusion is untouched for vac+2 (1/3 < Delta < 1, C8a), the squeezed vacuum (2/3) and Casimir (6/7) -- indeed for every zero-mean Gaussian state (the tree's T1, Delta >= 1/3); and even in case (ii) the band is thin and sits beside a region where <:T00^2:> < 0 and Delta > 1 (27.4% of rho<0 cells), diverging at <:T00^2:> = 0. KF's Fig. 2 caption 'Otherwise, Delta ~ 1' and C5 (printed (3.19) gives 0.9976 at the exact zero) are consistent with the figures having been drawn from (3.19) as printed; that is inference, not established (figures not viewed). So M's hypothesis is CONFIRMED in a specific, non-empirical form for this result -- a computation the authors did not have correct, not data they could not have had -- and having it changes the universal conclusion but not the generic one.
grade_evidence: Graded on the statement as the tree uses it: 'fluctuations of order unity wherever rho < 0 -- SURVIVES in every case they study' (fluctuation.py:63-64), KF_QUALITATIVE_CONCLUSION_SURVIVES = True (fluctuation.py:152, :480), with Delta the pointwise KF (3.2). A refuting counterexample is SHOWN, in a case KF study and inside their own plotted slice: the squeezed coherent state D(alpha)S(zeta)|0> with r = 1, alpha = 0.32876 (gamma = delta = 0), at theta = pi/2 has rho = -0.432332 K < 0 and <:T00^2:> = rho^2 exactly, so Delta = 0 -- by closed-form sympy along the whole curve s^2 = (1-e^{-2r})/8 (C3) and by independent truncated-Fock matrices (Delta = 4.5e-16, C4); z3 finds rho<0 with Delta = 0 and with Delta < 1/10 (C6). This is not a misprint: it is computed from KF's state family (3.9) and definition (3.2) alone and does not use any printed KF formula. KF's own universal sentences (abstract 'in all cases studied ... whenever', III.B 'we always have that Delta is at least of order unity') fail for case (ii); the tree never computed case (ii) on rho<0 (drift 1). Weight both ways, not in M's favour: (a) the conclusion STANDS, narrowed, for vac+2 (z3), the squeezed vacuum (2/3), Casimir (6/7) and every zero-mean Gaussian state (tree's T1); (b) in case (ii) it fails only on a codimension-one surface with a thin neighbourhood (Delta<0.1 on 0.9% of the slice's rho<0 cells), next to a region where <:T00^2:> < 0 and Delta > 1 -- so what survives is 'generically of order unity on rho < 0', not 'wherever'; (c) the tree already refuses pointwise Delta as a demand row (fluctuation.py:105-120, PRICES_THE_CORRIDOR = False, LEDGER_ROW_MOVES = False), so no ledger row moves on this finding; what rests on it is the printed M-D65-3 why-cell clause (ledger.py:871-872, 1073-1076, 3590-3596), which quotes the flag. Nothing is repaired. what_would_change_the_grade: To NARROWED: reading KF's 'at least of order unity' / 'whenever' as a generic (almost-everywhere-in-parameter-space) claim rather than a universal pointwise one -- the tree's wording 'wherever rho < 0' is universal, so this would need the tree's use restated, not new evidence. To STANDS: only a different measure than (3.2) (e.g. a smeared or non-normal-ordered Delta, or the full tensor (3.1) over all components) under which the t = 2 surface is not a zero -- that would be a different result. Against the counterexample itself: an error in the normal-ordered generating function or in the Fock control (both are in the script; they agree to 1e-15), or a KF squeezed-state family that excludes the witness (it does not: D(alpha)S(zeta)|0> with all complex alpha, zeta covers every single-mode pure Gaussian state, and the witness is on KF's plotted slice gamma = delta = 0, theta = pi/2). A later paper that already records this surface would change nothing in the grade, only its novelty.
